demos.title: Basics
demos.description: Every chart kind the library ships, [b]one cell at least[/b] each - bar fills four cells (plain, grouped, stacked, and one more carrying the reference lines) and area two (plain, stacked), as variants of one kind - and every mark appears here: bar, line, area, bubble scatter, range area, pie, donut, radar, violin, box, candlestick, heatmap, treemap, sunburst, sankey, chord, gauge, funnel, waffle, timeline, lollipop, milestone and the [b]reference-line mark[/b] ([code]SectionMark[/code]). Each cell is a [b]ChartView[/b] node with its kind, rows and field names set in the scene, so it can be copied and edited. Hover a chart for its tooltip; knobs that need code live in the three mark-knob pages, and a data transform (a histogram) in the custom-charts page.

demos.title: Dynamic data
demos.description: Two live charts running at [b]different rates[/b], each with a bounded buffer, plus a live gauge: an [b]oscilloscope[/b] at 60 Hz fed by a fixed-size [b]ring buffer[/b] (its axis stays pinned at 0..N, so the trace slides smoothly), a [b]price feed[/b] that appends one 10 second candle every 10 s through [code]AddRow[/code] + [code]WindowSize[/code] (the library drops the bars leaving the window; a time-label X axis never re-rounds) and a GaugeMark showing the newest sample. Space pauses, 1 / 2 change the speed of both feeds, C clears.

demos.title: ChartView fields (code)
demos.description: Every [b]ChartView[/b] knob, set from code: the six data channels with their ranges, four of the five [code]ColorMapping[/code] kinds (the fifth, [code]Auto[/code], is the default this page leaves alone), pinned axis domains, the [b]Light[/b] palette next to a [b]theme resource built in code[/b], axes with units and the legend, and every data entry point ([code]SetValues[/code] / [code]SetData[/code] / [code]SetCsv[/code]+[code]ParseCsv[/code] / [code]AddRow[/code]+[code]WindowSize[/code] / [code]Clear[/code]) plus [code]Refresh()[/code] versus [code]Repaint()[/code].

demos.title: ChartView hooks (code)
demos.description: The remaining [b]ChartView[/b] escape hatches: [code]ConfigureMark[/code], two tooltip content builders (plain text and rich spans), one canvas shared by two views through [code]CanvasFactory[/code] with the [code]Surface[/code] -> [code]Canvas[/code] -> [code]Texture[/code] triple presented by a TextureRect, and the editor-only [code]EditorPreview[/code] switch. [code]ConfigureChart[/code] itself, [code]Refresh[/code] vs [code]Repaint[/code] and the five events live on the [b]ChartViewFieldsDemo[/b] and [b]ChartCallbacksDemo[/b] pages.

demos.title: Events and interaction (code)
demos.description: The five [b]Chart[/b] events (hover, click, selection, focus, legend click) with their payloads logged live, the interaction verbs ([code]Select[/code] / [code]FocusSeries[/code] / [code]HideSeries[/code] / [code]ShowSeries[/code] / [code]ToggleSeriesVisibility[/code] / [code]ShowAllSeries[/code]) driven by buttons, an [b]external legend[/b] built from [code]GetSeriesInfo[/code], and a hand-written pointer loop over [code]HitTest[/code] / [code]Interaction[/code] / [code]NotifyHoverChanged[/code] ([code]Hover(row)[/code] is the silent variant and is deliberately not called).

demos.title: Animation (code)
demos.description: Host-driven animation: [code]AnimationController[/code]'s entry, hover, data-transition and exit phases through [code]AnimationContext[/code], the seven [code]EaseType[/code] curves drawn by a custom mark (no built-in mark consumes [code]SeriesProgress[/code] or [code]DataTransitionProgress[/code]), and a theme whose [code]EnableAnimation[/code] the host honours - or ignores.

demos.title: Theme surface (code)
demos.description: The [b]ChartTheme[/b] surface group by group: palette and gradient, frame colours, typography, line widths and tooltip metrics, the [code]Enable*[/code] toggles, [code]Clone()[/code] next to [code]Dark()[/code] and [code]Light()[/code], editing the resource live, and [b]Chart[/b] colour overrides.

demos.title: Custom charts (code)
demos.description: Hand-built charts without [code]ChartView[/code], which is also where the two forms it cannot express live: a full [b]second value axis[/b] ([code]Encode[/code] + [code]Scale[/code] + [code]Y2Axis[/code] + [code]ScaleDomain[/code]), five marks including three custom ones, [code]Mark<T>()[/code] / [code]ApplyToAllMarks[/code] / [code]Transform(IDataTransform)[/code], the built-in [b]BinTransform[/b] (the histogram cell), mark-level encodings, local data, style callbacks, element states and labels. The seven renderer slots are ChartRendererDemo's subject.

demos.title: Scales (code)
demos.description: Ten of the library's twelve [code]IScale[/code] implementations on hand-built charts ([code]LogScale[/code] has a cell of its own on the custom-charts page, and [code]OutputRangeScale[/code] is the one [code]ChartView[/code] uses internally for a pinned axis range): [b]TimeScale[/b], [b]SequentialColorScale[/b], [b]OrdinalScale[/b] + [b]ColorScale[/b] + [b]ShapeScale[/b], [b]IdentityColorScale[/b], [b]DivergingColorScale[/b], and [b]BandScale[/b] / [b]RadialScale[/b] consumed by two custom marks - no built-in mark reads those two.

demos.title: Canvas and host loop (code)
demos.description: Host integration: hit testing and click handling that drive selection and focus, series visibility from code (H / L hot keys), row appends through both [code]AppendData[/code] overloads (A / B hot keys - the new category grows the axis by itself), the read-only queries on the status line, one [code]Canvas2DFactory[/code] canvas shared by two [b]Chart[/b] consumers and presented by a TextureRect, and both flavours of [code]Dispose[/code]. Dynamic data lives on the ChartStreamingDemo page.

demos.title: Renderer slots (code)
demos.description: All seven renderer slots replaced together with the page's own implementations (background, title, grid, axis, axis labels, legend, crosshair) and switched back to the defaults with one more click; the canvas API in full (paths, paint state, dashes, gradients, transforms, clipping, [code]MeasureText[/code], [code]DrawImage[/code], capabilities); and a hit-test-driven overlay that the host paints itself.

demos.title: Real data: 24 countries (code)
demos.description: A chart a reader actually asks for: the World Bank's annual population growth ([code]SP.POP.GROW[/code]) for 24 major countries over every year from 1970 to 2023 - 1296 rows loaded from a shipped CSV through [code]SetCsv[/code], one series and one colour per country. [b]Wheel[/b] zooms the X axis around the pointer, [b]drag[/b] pans it, [b]double click[/b] resets, and a click on a [b]legend[/b] entry hides or shows that country. The growth rate (percent) is what makes countries of very different size comparable on one Y axis. [b]D[/b] / [b]Z[/b] / [b]B[/b] / [b]X[/b] set the decimation mode, the wheel's zoom factor, the pan button and the double-click reset; the readout names the current value of each.

demos.title: Layered rendering (code)
demos.description: The same table and the same [b]LineMark[/b] rendered two ways, side by side: the left chart draws every frame in a single pass, the right one keeps its data layer in an image ([code]Chart.UseLayerCache[/code], reached from a page as [code]LayeredRendering = true[/code]) and repaints only the overlay. [b]1[/b]/[b]2[/b]/[b]3[/b]/[b]4[/b] switch 1k-200k rows, [b]B[/b] measures 60 static redraws on both charts at once, [b]H[/b] measures 60 hover redraws, [b]S[/b] toggles [code]LineMark.Smooth[/code] and [b]A[/b] replays the entry animation - the frame a pointer move costs with and without the cache. Memory is reported twice and the sources are kept apart: the layer image is computed from the chart rectangle (width x height x 4 bytes, what the right chart costs extra), the per-row figure is measured with [code]GC.GetTotalMemory(true)[/code] around the table build.

demos.title: Layout and sizes (code)
demos.description: Where a chart's size comes from, on one [b]ChartView[/b] node: [code]Chart.MinimumSize[/code] - the title row, the legend, the X axis label row, the axis title row, the Y label column and the static [code]Chart.MinimumPlotSize[/code] added up - the size the layout around it gave the node, and the plot rectangle [code]Chart.CurrentPlotArea[/code] really got, with its four insets ([code]left = plot.X[/code], [code]right = size.X - (plot.X + plot.W)[/code], the same vertically). That difference is the layout budget, and every figure is read back from the public API a few frames after each key: [b]T[/b] toggles the title, [b]L[/b] walks the legend Top → Bottom → Left → Right → None, [b]A[/b] the X/Y axis titles, [b]Y[/b] a second Y axis (its reservation only - the node has no Y2 export, so the page builds that chain in [code]ConfigureChart[/code]), [b]F[/b] the theme's font size, and [b]M[/b] pins the node to [code]Chart.MinimumSize[/code] and then below it (×0.85 / ×0.70 / ×0.55, once more to let it fill the cell) - far enough and the axis thins its own labels with one warning in the editor Output. The [b]Δ[/b] line reports what the last key changed, and the hint compares the legend positions measured in the same state. [b]R[/b] / [b]S[/b] / [b]N[/b] / [b]P[/b] / [b]V[/b] / [b]W[/b] drive six more exports (label rotation, tick density, label formats, content shape, vertical alignment, pinned Y ends), each one named with its live value in the readout.

demos.title: Mark knobs: Cartesian (code)
demos.description: One cell per Cartesian mark, every knob named in the caption: [b]Interval[/b] (padding, corner radius, stacking - plain or normalised - and orientation - vertical or horizontal), [b]Line[/b] (smoothing, step mode, area, stroke width, the [b]stacked area[/b]), [b]Point[/b] (radius and size mapping), [b]RangeArea[/b], [b]Box[/b], [b]Candlestick[/b], [b]Heatmap[/b], [b]Timeline[/b], [b]Milestone[/b], [b]Lollipop[/b], [b]Violin[/b] and [b]Waffle[/b].

demos.title: Mark knobs: polar (code)
demos.description: The polar and proportion marks: [b]Pie[/b] (inner radius, start angle, explode, slice label builder), [b]Donut[/b] (centre text and a rich centre), [b]Gauge[/b] (sweep, arc width, ring form, label switches, track and value colours), [b]Radar[/b] (rings, grid, vertex dots, fill) and [b]Funnel[/b].

demos.title: Mark knobs: hierarchy and flow (code)
demos.description: The hierarchy and flow marks: [b]Treemap[/b] with both layout modes (binary split versus squarify), [b]Sunburst[/b] rings from parent rows, [b]Sankey[/b] column/node geometry and [b]Chord[/b] arcs - the field names are knobs here, not conventions.

demos.title: Geographic
demos.description: [b]A map file, drawn three ways[/b]. Assets/geo-regions.geojson - eight provinces read with [code]GeoJsonReader[/code] at runtime, no network - is joined to a small value table by name and shaded with a [code]SequentialColorScale[/code] in the first cell; the [b]same[/b] mark draws the [b]same[/b] features with [code]Shade = false[/code] as an outline-only base map in the second; and the third cell is the two-stage picture those two are for - that base map with a [code]GeoBubbleMark[/code] and a [code]GeoFlowMark[/code] over it, three layers reading three tables in one coordinate frame.
